title: Decode a stop code
description:
Write `describeBugCheck(code, parameters)`, which turns a bug check into a short summary for a crash report. `parameters` holds the four bug check parameters.

| Code | Return |
|---|---|
| `0x0A` | `"IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL: address 0x{p1} at IRQL {p2}"` |
| `0xD1` | `"DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL: address 0x{p1} at IRQL {p2}, code at 0x{p4}"` |
| `0x50` | `"PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA: {read or write} 0x{p1}"`, where parameter 2 is 0 for a read and anything else for a write |
| `0xC4` | `"DRIVER_VERIFIER_DETECTED_VIOLATION: rule 0x{p1}"` |
| `0x19` | `"BAD_POOL_HEADER"` |
| anything else | `"BUGCHECK 0x{code}"` |

Addresses and codes are written in upper-case hex without leading zeros; the IRQL in decimal. (`0x0A` and `0x19` as codes are written exactly as in the table's names, not formatted.)

```
describeBugCheck(0xD1, { 0x10, 2, 0, 0xFFFFF80612345678 })
  == "DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL: address 0x10 at IRQL 2, code at 0xFFFFF80612345678"
```
hints: A `switch` on the code with one `std::format` per case. `{:X}` writes upper-case hexadecimal without leading zeros; `{}` writes the IRQL in decimal.
lessonTitle: Why Kernel Bugs Take the Whole Machine Down
